summary: AgroPulse is a bilingual (English/Arabic) web app that helps farmers choose the next crop in their rotation. It fetches NASA climate and soil-wetness data for the farm's location and ranks nine crops with a transparent scoring model that explains every recommendation. By matching crops to local conditions and breaking pest and nutrient cycles, it supports soil health, saves water and builds resilience to climate change. Built for the Agriculture and Crop Rotation challenge by Team MMSS.
details:
WHAT IT DOES
AgroPulse is a decision-support web app for crop rotation. The farmer selects a location (or enters coordinates), soil type, previous crop and whether irrigation is available. The app retrieves NASA climate data for that location and ranks nine crops from 0 to 100, with a plain-language reason behind every score.

HOW IT WORKS
1) Live NASA data: precipitation, air temperature and root-zone soil wetness for the last three full years, via the NASA POWER API.
2) Transparent scoring: a rule-based model checks plant-family change (breaks pest and disease cycles), nitrogen balance (legumes after heavy feeders restore soil nitrogen), water supply vs crop need, temperature range and soil suitability.
3) Results: the top three crops with the reasons shown as checks and warnings. If the NASA service is unreachable, the app falls back to clearly labeled approximate demo values.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT
Healthier soil through smarter sequencing, less water waste by matching crops to local conditions, fewer pest outbreaks and lower input costs. The app works on phones and computers, needs no installation or account, and is available in English and Arabic to reach more farmers.

TOOLS
HTML, CSS and JavaScript in a single page, hosted free on GitHub Pages. NASA POWER API for data. An AI assistant (Claude) helped write code and text; all was reviewed and tested by the team.

CREATIVITY
Instead of a black-box prediction, every recommendation is explainable, so a farmer can see why a crop was suggested and challenge it. The tool is bilingual and works offline-safe with a fallback mode.

FACTORS CONSIDERED
Crop parameters are simplified agronomic values and the model is a prototype, not a yield forecast. Recommendations should be validated with local agronomists. Next steps: add SMAP soil moisture, and train a yield-prediction model on public data (FAOSTAT or USDA).
